entry.title: Housing · Mon, Jul 20, 2026
entry.summary:
Adopted: Roanoke Redevelopment and Housing Authority Annual Report. The Roanoke Redevelopment and Housing Authority presented its annual report covering the period from July 1, 2025, to June 30, 2026, which Council received and filed via the consent agenda. Recorded vote: 7-0.
Adopted: HUD Entitlement Funds Acceptance and Appropriation for Program Year 2026. The City Council adopted an ordinance accepting and appropriating Program Year 2026 Entitlement Funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) for the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG), HOME Investment Partnership, and Emergency Solutions Grant (ESG) programs. Recorded vote: 7-0.

entry.title: Housing · Mon, Jul 6, 2026
entry.summary:
Adopted: Amendments to Chapter 36.2 Zoning Code for Housing Development and Land Use. Following the continuation of a public hearing, the City Council adopted an ordinance and a resolution approving proposed amendments to Chapter 36.2 (Zoning) of the Code of the City of Roanoke. The amendments are intended to facilitate context-sensitive housing development, promote community health and wellness, encourage purposeful land use, update use tables for multiple purpose, industrial, and planned unit development districts, and clarify and correct zoning code elements. Recorded vote: 7-0.

entry.title: Housing · Mon, Jun 15, 2026
entry.summary:
Adopted: Bond Issuance for Westwood Village Apartments. Council adopted a resolution approving the issuance of bonds by the Roanoke Redevelopment and Housing Authority to help finance the Westwood Village Apartments multifamily housing complex. Recorded vote: 6-0.

entry.title: Housing · Mon, Jun 1, 2026
entry.summary:
Hearing scheduled: Continuation of Public Hearing on Comprehensive Zoning Code Amendments. City Council voted 6-0 to continue the May 18 public hearing on proposed amendments to Chapter 36.2 (Zoning) to July 6, 2026, at 7:00 pm. The proposed amendments address context-sensitive housing development, community health and wellness, use tables for multiple purpose, industrial, and planned unit development districts, and zoning code clarifications. Recorded vote: 6-0.
Official source: https://roanokeva.api.civicclerk.com/v1/Meetings/GetMeetingFileStream(fileId=6491,plainText=false)

entry.title: Housing · Mon, May 18, 2026
entry.summary:
Adopted: Real Property Tax Exemption for 2750 Hoover Street and 1729 Patterson Avenue. Council adopted Ordinance No. 43400-051826 granting real property tax exemption requests for properties owned by Villa Heights Rec Center, LLC and 1729 Patterson Avenue, LLC (operated under Restoration Housing). Recorded vote: 6-1.
Deferred: Citywide Zoning Code Amendments (Chapter 36.2). A public hearing was held on proposed citywide amendments to Chapter 36.2 (Zoning) intended to promote context-sensitive housing, community health, and revise district use tables; City Council postponed the matter to a subsequent meeting.

entry.title: Housing · Mon, Aug 17, 2026
entry.summary:
Adopted: HUD Continuum of Care Grant for Homeless Assistance Team. City Council adopted an ordinance accepting and appropriating the FY 2025 HUD Continuum of Care Grant Award for the Homeless Assistance Team (HAT). Recorded vote: 6-0.
Adopted: HUD Continuum of Care Grant for Coordinated Assessment System. City Council adopted an ordinance accepting and appropriating the FY 2025 HUD Continuum of Care Grant Award for the Coordinated Assessment System (CAS). Recorded vote: 6-0.
Adopted: HUD Continuum of Care Planning Grant Acceptance and Appropriation. City Council adopted an ordinance accepting and appropriating the FY 2025 HUD Continuum of Care Grant Award for CoC Planning. Recorded vote: 6-0.
Discussion / report: Staff Follow-Up on Historic Gainsboro Home Rehab Funding. Staff reported on follow-up discussions regarding ARPA funding for home rehabilitation in Historic Gainsboro, specifically 23 Gilmer Avenue. Officials explained the home did not meet grant guidelines because it was not owner-occupied when applied for, is uninhabitable, and requires repairs—including a foundation—exceeding funding by hundreds of thousands of dollars. A site visit was arranged to assess total costs.

entry.title: Housing · Mon, Oct 19, 2026
entry.summary:
Discussion / report: Lead Poisoning Prevention Week Proclamation. Mayor Joseph L. Cobb presented a proclamation declaring October 25–31, 2026, as National Lead Poisoning Prevention Week to Housing Programs and Policy Manager Desi Wynter, Lead Safe Roanoke Program Manager Katie Kennedy, and attending staff.
Discussion / report: Roanoke Neighborhood Advocates Annual Report. Representatives from Roanoke Neighborhood Advocates and the Neighborhood Services Coordinator presented the board's annual report and activities to City Council.
Adopted: Rezoning of 0 Janette Avenue SW. Following a public hearing, City Council voted 7-0 to adopt Ordinance No. 43486-101926, rezoning 0 Janette Avenue SW from Recreation and Open Space District (ROS) to Residential District (RM-2). Recorded vote: 7-0.
Adopted: Rezoning of Parcels at 0 Franklin Road SW. Following a public hearing, City Council voted 7-0 to adopt Ordinance No. 43487-101926, approving the request of Lawson Company Incorporated to rezone three parcels at 0 Franklin Road SW from Mixed Use District (MX) to Residential District (RM-2). Recorded vote: 7-0.
